“C'est peut-être vrai dès que $Y$ est noethérien” concerns finite **relative** cohomological dimension of $f_*$, in the surrounding finite-type discussion, rather than finite absolute cohomological dimension of $Y$. The finite-type-over-a-field case has a direct modern counterpart (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10)), and Illusie (2014, Exposé XVIII_A, Corollary 1.4) proves the relative $\ell$-torsion statement for finite-dimensional noetherian $Y$ with $\ell$ invertible on $Y$. Those results confirm qualified versions; these notes leave the draft's full “merely noetherian” scope unresolved and do not offer the absolute cohomology of a field as a counterexample to it.

The words “d'additivité pour un mapping cylindre” should be read with their chain-level compatibility data, not promoted to additivity for every endomorphism of an abstract distinguished triangle. The latter statement is false even for perfect complexes: The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., [Tag 087L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087L), Lemma 110.65.1) gives a counterexample. This is a boundary for a possible modern reconstruction, not a contradiction of what the manuscript actually states.
**Confidence:** high — the stronger false statement and a primary counterexample are explicitly identified.

The typed parenthesis “then $R=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$” is not a consequence of equal characteristic and a regular system of parameters alone: $R=\mathbb Q[x,y]_{(x,y)}$ is countable and has coefficient field $\mathbb Q$, whereas $\mathbb Q[[x,y]]$ is uncountable. The primary complete-local theorem explicitly assumes completeness (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0C0S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C0S)). This is a conditional counterexample to the isolated wording, and the right next step is to recover earlier conventions from the reused source before declaring its full theorem false.
**Confidence:** high for the counterexample; unresolved whether the earlier source imposed completeness throughout.

The lemma lifting a generator through a surjection of finite cyclic groups is proved across 143 and 141, so its proof should be read in the reused source's printed order. It concerns a finite cyclic group and the arithmetic of exponents, whereas **LM4 D.12** and **LM4 F.7** concern full profinite torsion/centralizer questions. The overlap in finite-group vocabulary supplies no proof, counterexample or change of status for either open register entry.
### N54. The literal étale criterion admits a dual-number counterexample

In condition (c), finite separability of $\kappa(y)/\kappa(x)$ alone does not imply the subsequent equality $m_y=m_xO_y$: $\operatorname{Spec}(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2)\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite, flat and finitely presented, with residue extension $k/k$, but has $m_y=(\varepsilon)\ne0$. Its nonreduced fibre prevents étaleness, in agreement with the criterion requiring étale fibres (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 03PC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03PC), Proposition 59.26.2). This is a counterexample to the isolated residue-field-only wording as transcribed, not to the stronger condition printed immediately afterward or to an unseen theorem elsewhere.
